title: Support for parents
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:33Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers children and court decisions after parental separation under the Family Law Act, not support services such as family, friends, maternal and child health nurses and parenting services for new parents, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Support for parents
card: New parents can get help from many places. Support can be practical, such as meals or babysitting, or emotional, such as someone to listen.
informal support. They can help with daily tasks, give advice from their own experience and offer company.
nurses in Victoria's free Maternal and Child Health Service. They check a baby's growth and development and give advice on feeding, sleep and parent wellbeing.
organisations such as helplines, parenting groups and early parenting centres. They offer advice and programs to help parents build skills and confidence.
draft.remember: Support can come from people close to parents or from trained services, and both can help parents cope.

a.q: Which is an example of practical support for a new parent?
opts: A neighbour cooks dinner for the family twice a week
A friend says they understand how tiring it feels
A relative tells the parent they are doing well
A cousin phones each night to ask how the day went
a.why: Cooking meals is practical help because it takes a daily task off the parent. The other options are mainly emotional support, such as listening and encouragement.
a.clue: Which one helps by doing a task for the parent?

b.q: Priya is worried that her baby in Bendigo is not feeding well. She wants advice from someone trained to check the baby's growth. Who is the best source?
opts: A maternal and child health nurse
A friend who has two young children
Her parents, who raised three children
A parenting group on a social media page
b.why: Maternal and child health nurses are trained to check growth and development and to advise on feeding. Friends and family can give comfort and experience, but they are not trained to assess the baby, so they are not the best fit here.
b.clue: Look for the person trained to check a baby's growth.

a.best: A neighbour cooks dinner for the family twice a week

b.best: A maternal and child health nurse
